intro: Rules for the seven playable classes. Changelog lines are quoted in the rules below. Evolution chains, synergies, passives, scaling, and item-mod notes are a separate section read from the public game client and are not tested in play. No D2 Survivors build guides are published yet, so this page does not recommend builds. The game changes often.
classesNote: The game site describes all seven heroes. They are Amazon, Sorceress, Necromancer, Paladin, Barbarian, Druid and Assassin. Warlock is not in the game.

general.title: Skill slots
paragraphs: A run starts as in D2, with only Attack and your starting weapon. The first card comes at once: a first skill from each skill tree, so all six skill slots are yours to fill.
A run started on Nightmare or Hell has its skill and passive slots from the start: 8 and 8 on Nightmare, 10 and 10 in Hell.
An earlier build said each difficulty adds two more skill slots and two more passive slots.

cites.quote: A run starts as in D2, with only Attack and your starting weapon, and your first card comes at once: a first skill from each skill tree, so all six skill slots are yours to fill

general.title: Lowering resistance
paragraphs: -% to Enemy Resistance lowers a monster's resistance, as in D2, instead of adding damage.
Monsters resist each element by D2's numbers, and immunities break only as D2's do: Amplify Damage, Decrepify, Lower Resist and Conviction lower resistances, a fifth as much on an immune.

paragraphs: The changelog flipped this on the same day. The later line is the one that still stands: gear works at any level again. An item's Required Level is shown, but it no longer holds the item back.
The earlier line that day said gear asks its D2 Required Level again: you can wear it at any level, but above yours it shows red and gives nothing until you reach it.

tip.label: Fan tip, not a changelog rule
paragraphs: For a straightforward first run, try Barbarian and choose Double Swing when the skill choices appear.

Attacks such as Double Swing fire automatically, so focus on making room around enemies and collecting nearby drops. As you level up, read the choices and select an upgrade that supports your current skills.

sections.title: Slots and level caps
paragraphs: Skill slots and passive slots are separate: 6 and 6 on Normal, 8 and 8 on Nightmare, 10 and 10 in Hell.
Active skills stop at level 8, passives at 5 (Telekinesis at 3), and an evolved skill at 1.
A skill cannot rise above character level minus its required level, plus 1. A skill that requires level R reaches 8 only once the character is at least R+7.

sections.title: Level-up cards
paragraphs: Each level-up shows 3 cards: a new skill while a skill slot is free, +1 to a skill or passive you already have, or a new passive while a passive slot is free.
A run has 2 rerolls, 2 skips, and 2 banishes.

A passive that would evolve a skill you own is offered four times as often. +1 to a skill that can evolve is twice as likely, or four times once you hold its catalyst. When free passive slots are no more than the catalysts you still need, the only new passives offered are those catalysts. Necromancer curses are offered at 0.4 times the usual weight.

The first offer is one level-1 damage skill from each tree. Paladin always starts with Blessed Hammer, and Barbarian always starts with Double Swing. In Hell, fire skills are left out of that starting offer when another choice exists.

sections.title: Evolution
paragraphs: A skill evolves when it is at its max level, you own its catalyst passive at any level, and your character level meets the required level of both the evolved skill and the catalyst. The next chest performs the evolution. The evolved skill starts at level 1, which is its max, and its cooldown resets.
A further step only needs the next catalyst and that step's level requirement.

Some catalysts are the general passives Faster Cast Rate, Faster Run/Walk, Vitality, and Replenish Life. Where the earliest character level is higher than the required level, both are shown on the class.

sections.title: +skills
paragraphs: Effective level is the base level, plus All Skills, plus Fire, Cold, or Lightning Skills when the skill is that element, plus skill-tree bonuses, plus a bonus to that one skill. It is not capped at 8.
Evolved skills only grow through +skills. Each extra level is worth the larger of 15% more, or continuing the damage curve of the skill it replaced.
Passives, including Paladin auras, also gain All Skills and tree bonuses. The changelog line above is the published note; this paragraph is the client formula.

sections.title: Synergies
paragraphs: A listed synergy is halved and rounded, per level of the source skill. Listed 12 is about 6% per level, listed 15 is about 8%, and listed 3 is about 2%.
Meteor and Blizzard use a D2-style scale: listed percent, times one half, times 20 divided by the source skill's max level. Those resulting percents are medium confidence.
A skill you evolved away from still counts as its max level for synergy. An evolved skill keeps the synergy list of the skill it replaced.

sections.title: Item mods
paragraphs: Enhanced Damage becomes attack damage at 40% of the listed figure, so 100% enhanced damage is +40% attack damage. A max-damage percent on a caster weapon is ignored.
Increased Attack Speed counts as half as much faster cast rate, because skills run on cooldowns.

Enhanced Defense becomes damage reduction of 15 times the natural log of (1 + enhanced defense / 100), in percent. A flat “Damage Reduced by N” becomes N/3 percent. Damage reduction from these stops at 50%.

A skill-tab bonus adds levels to one tree. Its index is the class index times 3, plus the tree, minus 1, with classes ordered Amazon, Sorceress, Necromancer, Paladin, Barbarian, Druid, Assassin. “+N to Class Skills” adds to all three of that class's trees. Fire, Cold, or Lightning Skills add to that element.

A charge of a skill auto-casts on a timer: the longer of that skill's cooldown at the charged level, or 60 seconds divided by the number of charges, then scaled by cast speed. The cast level cannot pass the skill's max, and it gets no synergies.

A proc on hit, on attack, or when struck is a percent chance to cast, at most once every 0.35 seconds for that proc. The level is capped at the skill's max, there are no synergies, and the skill can belong to another class.
Skills cast from gear — charges and procs — get no synergies and are capped at their max level. An aura mod runs that Paladin aura, capped at the aura's max level.
